verdict.rationale: Martin documents a dedicated 'background tasks' category where it works asynchronously on your behalf. Examples include Cc'ing Martin to schedule a meeting, proactive email drafts, email triage with follow-up actions, and recurring briefings, and custom shortcuts can trigger multi-step actions. However, these are fixed, predefined task types rather than open-ended delegation of an arbitrary multi-step task, and a 'returns for my review' checkpoint is only implied by drafting. Missing for 10: documented general-purpose delegation of arbitrary multi-step tasks to run autonomously, an explicit review/approval handoff before completion, task status or progress visibility, and hands-on corroboration of long-running background work.
